translations.literal: More than three thousand exiles were settled in Qian and lived intermixed with Miao people, where quarrels easily arose; he memorialized to transfer them to Xinjiang;
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand exiles had been settled in Guizhou among the Miao, where friction was constant; he memorialized to send them to Xinjiang instead;

sentences.zh: 又以鎮遠、黎平、都勻、古州苗俗桀驁，以盜為生，州縣差役緝捕難週，疏請綠營每百名內精選數名，分隸府、廳、州、縣文員管轄，勤加訓練，專司捕盜：並下部議行。

translations.literal: He also noted that in Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou Miao customs were fierce and unruly and they lived by robbery; county runners could not pursue comprehensively; he memorialized to select several elite men from every hundred Green Standard troops, assign them to civil officials of prefectures, departments, and counties, train them diligently, and specialize in capturing bandits—all referred to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Miao in Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were fierce and lived by robbery, which county runners could not suppress; he proposed selecting elite Green Standard soldiers from every hundred, assigning them to civil officials in each district, training them, and specializing them in bandit-catching—all of which was referred to the ministry for approval.

sentences.zh: 長齡治黔九載，振興文教，貴陽、銅仁、安順、石阡四府，普安、八寨、郎岱、松桃四廳，黃平、普定，天柱、永從、甕安、清平、興義、普安諸州縣，皆建書院義學；

translations.literal: Changling governed Qian for nine years and revived culture and education; in the four prefectures of Guiyang, Tongren, Anshun, and Shiqian, the four departments of Pu'an, Bazhai, Langdai, and Songtao, and the districts of Huangping, Puding, Tianzhu, Yongcong, Weng'an, Qingping, Xingyi, Pu'an, and others, academies and charity schools were all established;
translations.idiomatic: In nine years governing Guizhou, Changling revived education; academies and charity schools were established in the prefectures of Guiyang, Tongren, Anshun, and Shiqian, the departments of Pu'an, Bazhai, Langdai, and Songtao, and in Huangping, Puding, Tianzhu, Yongcong, Weng'an, Qingping, Xingyi, Pu'an, and other districts;

sentences.zh: 省會書院分上內外三舍，親試考覈，刊刻經籍，頒行州縣。

translations.literal: the provincial academy was divided into upper, inner, and outer dormitories; he personally examined and evaluated students, printed classics, and distributed them to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: the provincial academy was divided into upper, inner, and outer halls; he examined students in person, printed classical texts, and distributed them through the province.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢雲貴總督，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general and concurrently acted as Yunnan governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently acted as governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 漢、回連歲互鬥，永昌回變敗退後，复圖攻城，城回謀內應，迤西道羅天池悉捕誅之。

translations.literal: Han and Hui fought each other year after year; after the Yongchang Hui rebellion failed and retreated, they again plotted to storm the city; city Hui conspired as inside collaborators and Yixi Circuit Intendant Luo Tianchi arrested and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Hui had fought year after year; after the Yongchang Muslim rising failed, the rebels again plotted to take the city, and Hui inside the walls conspired with them; Yixi Circuit Intendant Luo Tianchi arrested and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 長齡親往督剿，擊走叛回，以肅清入告。

translations.literal: Changling went in person to direct suppression, drove off the rebel Hui, and reported pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Changling went in person to direct operations, drove off the rebel Muslims, and reported that order had been restored.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，回眾藉口善良不別，复叛，自請議處，撤銷獎敘，赴大理、永昌督剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Hui masses, taking as pretext that good and bad were not distinguished, rebelled again; he requested punishment for himself, had his rewards revoked, and went to Dali and Yongchang to direct suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the Muslims rebelled again on the pretext that innocents had not been distinguished from guilty parties; he asked to be punished, gave up his rewards, and went to Dali and Yongchang to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 匪尋竄散，請免投誠張富罪，軍犯王芝異團練出力，亦請釋回。

translations.literal: The bandits soon fled and dispersed; he requested pardon for the surrendered Zhang Fu, and for the military convict Wang Zhiyi, who had aided the militia, also to be released.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon scattered; he asked that the surrendered Zhang Fu be pardoned and that Wang Zhiyi, a military convict who had helped the militia, be released as well.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其庸懦，降補河南布政使。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked his mediocrity and cowardice and demoted him to Henan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked his timidity and demoted him to provincial treasurer of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 滇回复擾雲州，多屬永昌遺孽，且得羅天池濫殺狀，追論長齡，褫職。

translations.literal: Yunnan Hui again harassed Yunzhou, mostly remnants of Yongchang; moreover the facts of Luo Tianchi's indiscriminate killing were obtained, Changling was pursued in review, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Muslim unrest broke out again in Yunzhou, largely among Yongchang remnants; when Luo Tianchi's indiscriminate killings came to light, Changling was called to account and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒。

translations.literal: After a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳若霖、戴三錫盡心民事，而三錫久任蜀疆，治效較多。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Chen Ruolin and Dai Sanxi devoted themselves to the people's affairs, but Sanxi served long on the Shu frontier and achieved more in governance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Chen Ruolin and Dai Sanxi both devoted themselves to public welfare, but Sanxi's long service in Sichuan produced the greater results.

sentences.zh: 孫爾準、程祖洛先後治閩有聲，寬嚴殊途，其相濟之道乎？

translations.literal: Sun Erzhun and Cheng Zuluo successively governed Fujian with reputation; lenient and strict were different paths—is this their way of complementing one another?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Erzhun and Cheng Zuluo each governed Fujian with distinction; one lenient, one strict—was that how they complemented each other?

sentences.zh: 裕泰兩殄楚寇，勳施爛然。

translations.literal: Yu Tai twice exterminated Chu bandits; his merit shone brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tai twice crushed bandits in Huguang, and his achievements shone brightly.

sentences.zh: 賀長齡儒而不武，不足以奠岩疆也。

translations.literal: He Changling was scholarly but not martial, insufficient to secure a rugged frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He Changling was a scholar rather than a soldier, and was not equal to securing a hard frontier.
